paper.title_en: Hybrid Expansion Cosmology in f(T) Gravity: Late-Time Evolution and Observational Bounds
paper.abstract_en: The cosmological expansion history of the exponential $f(T)$ gravity model proposed by Linder is determined from a modified Friedmann equation that generally does not admit a closed-form analytical solution for the Hubble parameter, requiring repeated numerical evaluations in cosmological analyses. Motivated by this limitation, we present an analytical reconstruction of the model by introducing a Lambert--W-based hybrid expansion ansatz for the Hubble parameter. The free parameters of the reconstruction are first determined through a least-squares optimization by minimizing the deviation from the numerical solution of the modified Friedmann equation, yielding a maximum relative difference of approximately $1.08\%$ over the redshift range $0\leq z\leq4$. The reconstructed model is subsequently treated as an independent analytical cosmological model and constrained using recent late-time observations, including Cosmic Chronometer (CC), DESI DR2 Baryon Acoustic Oscillation (BAO), Pantheon+SH0ES, and Union3 Type Ia supernova datasets through Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) analyses. The resulting parameter constraints are mutually consistent across the individual datasets and become significantly tighter for the combined likelihood. Furthermore, various cosmological diagnostics demonstrate that the reconstructed model successfully describes the transition from an early decelerated universe to the present accelerated epoch while remaining in close agreement with the standard $Λ$CDM cosmology at late times. These results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid ansatz accurately reproduces the numerical exponential $f(T)$ expansion history while providing a computationally efficient analytical framework for cosmological parameter estimation and future observational studies.
